evidence: effortField splits on \n and trims \r, so CRLF files are read correctly. An empty file yields [""], which fails the opening-fence check without panicking.
slices.Index(lines[1:], "---") returns an offset into the subslice. lines[1:end+1] therefore covers exactly the frontmatter lines between the fences and excludes the closing fence.

Each table case traces to its expected result. For the no-newline closing fence, lines is [---, name: x, ---], end is 1, and no effort key is found, so the result is ("", true). The two missing-fence cases return false.
The regex does not match effort_level or a commented key such as '# effort:'. It matches indented, quoted and space-before-colon keys, as the commit claims.
